full_judgment:
3. The plaintiff-respondent filed the suit in respect of the schedule 'A' of the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit land was khas land of the Government and the same was leased out to the petitioners by the then Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Rajshahi, permanently on receipt of 'premium in Naogaon Settlement Case No.2325 of 1968-69. The possession of the suit land was duly handed over to the petitioner and a Kabuliyat was executed and registered on 28.11.1977. Although in the comment column of C.S. and S.A. Khatian of the suit property it was mentioned as "Peer's Dargabari" but, in fact, since long there has been no such Dargabari in the suit property and no religious rites and ceremonies were performed in the suit property and the said land has been in continuous use as a cultivable land and the plaintiff since his lease has been possessing and enjoying the suit property by cultivating paddy and other crops therein. Recently local enemical persons, the defendant Nos.4- 7 filed an objection to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon for cancellation of the permanent settlement of the plaintiff stating that the suit land is a religious property. The said objection has been registered as Miscellaneous Case No.2/X111/198-82 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon wherein the C.O. (Revenue), Neamatpur was directed to submit a spot inquiry report of the suit property. The C.O. (Revenue), Neamatpur submitted his report mentioning that the suit property was not a religious property and it is cultivable land. But. without considering the said report Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon, cancelled the permanent settlement of the plaintiff through order dated 30.10.1984. The plaintiff, thereafter, preferred an appeal before the Divisional Commissioner Rajshahi who affirmed the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Naogaon, by his order dated 04.11.1989. The further case of the plaintiff is that he did not violate. any of the terms and conditions of the lease deed of the permanent settlement and was competent under the law when he obtained the lease as he had not more than 2.30 acres of land. 

 7. It appears from the record, that ADC (Revenue), Rajshahi granted permanent lease in the year 1968769 on proper legal verification realized premium and subsequently rent froth the plaintiff was realized on putting him into possession of the suit land. A Kabuliyat containing certain terms and conditions relating to permanent settlement was obtained from the leasee-plaintiff. Subsequently R.S. record of right was prepared in the name of the plaintiff and he has been paying the rent regularly.
